[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

Both the Studio build plane and the Portal serve plane provide AI-assisted contextual help powered by the Assistive Guidance bounded context. A unified **Help Context** schema governs what information is assembled and passed to the AI Gateway for both planes. The context is assembled **locally in the browser** (no server round-trip to collect it), then sent as the system prompt prefix to the AI. Help sessions are **scoped to the current page and field** — context resets on navigation. Field-level help answers questions about a specific field; page-level help answers questions about the whole page, its purpose, and available actions. Conversations are **conversational** (multi-turn within the scoped session) using the Tier 2 model (Haiku-class). All help text and AI responses are localized to the user's active locale.

---
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#context-and-problem-statement]

## Context and Problem Statement

**Business Context:** Portal Studio is a complex authoring tool. Studio Designers and Admins need contextual guidance while configuring portals, managing components, setting up environments, and authoring pages — without leaving the current workflow to consult external documentation. Similarly, portal end users (Members, Providers, Caseworkers) need contextual help while completing tasks on deployed portals, grounded in the specific component or screen they are looking at.

**Technical Context:** The Assistive Guidance bounded context already owns AI-agent assistance in the conceptual architecture. It was scoped to the Portal serve plane (end-user help) and Studio authoring assistance (component scaffolding, wiring, completeness checking). This decision extends it to **field-level and page-level conversational help** on both planes, defining the context schema that grounds each help conversation.

**Problem Statement:** How is the AI context assembled for field-level and page-level help on both planes? What information is included? How is the conversation scoped and reset? How does the field `?` icon and page help panel (ADR-APP-018 §11) trigger a grounded AI conversation?
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- ⚡ Low latency — help must feel instant; context assembly must be client-side with no pre-fetch round-trip
- 🔒 No PHI in prompts — context must never include actual field values or API response data
- 🌐 Fully localized — questions and answers in the user's active locale
- 📋 Consistent pattern — same help invocation model on both planes; different context schemas

page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#unified-ai-help-context-model--two-context-schemas-one-invocation-pattern]

### Unified AI Help Context Model — Two Context Schemas, One Invocation Pattern
page_texts.9:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#help-invocation-pattern-both-planes]

#### Help Invocation Pattern (Both Planes)

Help is available at three levels, all using the same invocation and conversation UI:

| Level | Trigger | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **Field help** | Click/tap `?` icon adjacent to any form field label | Single field — purpose, valid values, effect, examples |
| **Page help** | Click "Ask AI" button in the page-level help panel | Full page — purpose, all fields, all actions, how-to guidance |
| **Floating help** | Persistent `?` chat button (bottom-right) available on every page | Current page context — general how-to, troubleshooting |

**Help UI component:** A slide-out panel (not a blocking modal) opens from the right edge of the screen with a chat interface. The panel is dismissible at any time. It does not block the underlying form — the user can continue editing while the panel is open. The chat thread persists for the current page session and clears on navigation.

**Help Mode — click any element to describe it:** When the help panel is open, the UI enters **Help Mode**. In Help Mode:
- A subtle pulsing ring appears on all interactive elements (fields, buttons, dropdowns, toggles) indicating they are "tappable for explanation"
- Clicking any field or UI element while in Help Mode automatically fires a pre-composed question to the AI: "Describe this field / action and explain how to use it" — with that element's context pre-loaded
- The AI immediately responds with a description of the element, its purpose, valid values, and how it affects the portal
- The user can then ask follow-up questions in the same chat thread
- Help Mode is indicated by a "Help Mode On" badge on the floating button and a light overlay on the page
- Help Mode exits automatically when the user closes the help panel or clicks the help button again

This interaction eliminates the need to type a question — the user simply opens help and clicks whatever they are curious about.

**Multi-turn conversation:** After the initial context-grounded question, the user can ask follow-up questions. Subsequent turns carry the full conversation history plus the original context prefix. The AI's answers are grounded in the context — it does not make up capabilities that do not exist on the current page.

page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#model-tier-assignment]

#### Model Tier Assignment

Per ADR-APP-014 Tier 2 (Standard / Haiku-class):

| Use case | Model alias | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Field help (Studio) | `portal-help` | Conversational; single question + answer |
| Page help (Studio) | `portal-help` | Conversational; how-to guidance |
| Component help (Portal) | `portal-help` | Conversational; end-user questions |
| Screen/page help (Portal) | `portal-help` | Conversational; task guidance |

Studio authoring assistance (component scaffolding, wiring generation) continues to use `studio-assist` (Tier 1 / Sonnet-class) — that is a separate higher-complexity task, not conversational help.

page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#context-assembly--client-side-no-round-trip]

#### Context Assembly — Client-Side, No Round-Trip

Context is assembled **entirely in the browser** from data already loaded on the page:

**Studio:** The `StudioHelpContext` is built from:
- The current route (from Next.js `usePathname`)
- The Studio actor role (from the session cookie)
- Static page metadata defined per-page (a `helpMeta` export from each page file)
- Field metadata from the Zod schema and the field's `helpText` prop (ADR-APP-018 §11)
- The current portal selection (from the portal context provider)

**Portal:** The `PortalHelpContext` is built from:
- The `PageAssembly` already loaded (contains persona, page, component contracts, help metadata)
- The active locale (from locale context)
- The component's declared `helpContent` slots (registered at component certification time)

No server round-trip is needed to assemble context — all the information is already in the browser from the initial page load.

---
page_texts.14:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#token-budget-and-rate-limiting]

#### Token Budget and Rate Limiting

- **Help conversations are token-budgeted per session** — the AI Gateway (ADR-SEC-007) enforces the Tier 2 token budget per session
- **Context prefix is compact** — the `StudioHelpContext` system prompt prefix is approximately 200–400 tokens; well within Haiku's context window
- **Conversation history is pruned** — if the conversation exceeds 10 turns, the oldest turns (beyond turn 3) are dropped from the history sent to the AI while the original context prefix is always retained

**Pros:**
- ✅ Grounded, relevant answers — AI cannot hallucinate features that do not exist on the current page
- ✅ No PHI exposure — context schema explicitly excludes all PHI and credential fields
- ✅ Low latency — client-side context assembly means no pre-fetch delay before the user sees the help panel
- ✅ Consistent UX — same invocation pattern, same slide-out panel, on both planes
- ✅ Localized — questions and answers match the user's active locale

**Cons:**
- ❌ Static page metadata (`helpMeta` exports) must be maintained as pages evolve
- ❌ Component help content quality depends on component developers declaring good `helpContent` slots

---
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#option-1-unified-context-schema-client-side-assembly-selected]

### Option 1: Unified Context Schema, Client-Side Assembly (Selected)

**Description:** Context assembled from in-browser state; sent to AI Gateway with compact system prompt prefix.

**Pros:** ✅ No round-trip; no PHI risk; consistent pattern on both planes

**Cons:** ❌ `helpMeta` per-page maintenance burden
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#option-2-server-side-context-assembly]

### Option 2: Server-Side Context Assembly

**Description:** When the user requests help, a Server Action fetches context from PostgreSQL (page structure, component contracts, etc.) before calling the AI.

**Pros:** ✅ Context is always fresh from the database

**Cons:** ❌ Adds 100–500ms latency before the help panel opens (poor UX); all this data is already on the client from the initial page load — no benefit
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#option-3-generic-help-no-pagefield-context]

### Option 3: Generic Help (No Page/Field Context)

**Description:** The AI receives only the user's question, no context about what page or field they are on.

**Pros:** ✅ No context schema to maintain

**Cons:** ❌ AI answers are generic and frequently wrong or unhelpful ("How do I set the form factor?" answered without knowing which page has that field); defeats the purpose of contextual help

---
page_texts.19:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Selected:** Option 1 — Unified context schema with client-side assembly on both planes.

---
page_texts.21:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#-positive]

### ✅ Positive

- Studio Designers get accurate, page-specific answers without leaving their authoring context
- Portal end users get component-specific guidance grounded in what they are actually looking at
- No PHI ever enters the AI inference pipeline via the help system
- Consistent help UX across the entire platform
page_texts.22:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#-negative]

### ❌ Negative

- Each Studio page must export a `helpMeta` object — adds a small maintenance surface
- Component developers must declare meaningful `helpContent` slots for portal help to be useful
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#-neutral]

### ⚪ Neutral

- Help conversations do not persist across page navigation — users start fresh on each page (intentional: prevents stale context from a prior page confusing the AI)

---
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#-risks]

### ⚠️ Risks

- Developer accidentally includes a PHI-adjacent field value in `currentValue` of `StudioHelpContext`
- AI answers a question about a feature that exists on a different page (context bleed)
- Component developers leave `helpContent` slots empty — poor portal help quality
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#-mitigations]

### 🛡️ Mitigations

- `StudioHelpContext` builder function (shared utility) controls which field values are safe to include; it uses a `safeValue()` helper that returns the value only for enum/boolean/numeric fields and returns `undefined` for free-text inputs
- System prompt explicitly instructs the AI to only describe features available on the current page and role; tested with adversarial prompts in integration tests
- Component certification gate (ADR-APP-008) requires at least one non-empty `helpContent` slot; components with empty help slots display a static fallback tooltip instead of triggering an AI conversation

---
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/PTN-APP-AI-001-ai-contextual-help-model.md#compliance-notes]

## Compliance Notes

- **HIPAA:** `PortalHelpContext` schema explicitly prohibits PHI fields. The `safeValue()` utility in `StudioHelpContext` prevents free-text field values from entering prompts. Both are application-layer invariants enforced in code (ADR-SEC-005 — no PHI in prompts).
- **Section 508:** The help panel and chat interface are fully keyboard accessible per ADR-APP-018. The floating help button meets the 44×44px touch target requirement.
- **Standards:**
  - ADR-APP-014 (this repo) — AI Inference Platform (Bedrock, Tier 2 model for help)
  - ADR-APP-018 (this repo) — UI/UX Standards §11 (field tooltips and page help panels — the entry points that trigger this ADR's help conversations)
  - ADR-SEC-007 (this repo) — AI Gateway security (token budget enforcement)
  - `eap-ref-architecture/strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/GUID-SEC-AI-APP-2.9.04.md` — Application-layer AI security (prompt injection prevention)
